That's not what concern trolling is. Concern trolling is interrupting a forum to raise concern for an irrelevant side-issue. Suppose Adam and Bob are arguing the merits of the assault gun ban. Adam is losing the argument. Rather than concede the point Adam makes a sock puppet, Connie. Connie interrupts with endless points-of-order about how Bob is going to alienate the press with the way he's phrasing things. The concern is as close as possible to something the community at large has already discussed and disagrees with itself about. The intent is to make the concern a larger issue than the debate, and generally disrupt the productivity of the forum.

Other examples are trolls on the Gamergate forums talking endlessly about whether or not to make a press release and people on Voat bitching endlessly about Amalek. If they can keep the focus on how bad a troll has to be before he's banned they will be keeping the focus off of things that make Voat a fun and engaging place to hang out.
